rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is on line 45 in the half-precision specialization `template<> __global__ void gelu_kernel<half>(...)`. With input dtype=torch.float32 (fixed per specification), `AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF` dispatches to `scalar_t = float`, invoking the generic template `gelu_kernel<float>` (lines 27-36), NOT the mutated half-precision specialization. The generic template's boundary check `if (idx < size)` on line 30 remains unchanged.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation specifically alters the boundary condition in the half-precision (float16) kernel specialization from `idx < size` to `idx < size - 1`. However, the input specification mandates dtype=torch.float32. When a float32 tensor is passed, PyTorch's `AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF` macro selects `scalar_t = float`, which uses the unmutated generic template `gelu_kernel<T>`. The half-precision specialization `gelu_kernel<half>` is only instantiated and called when the input tensor has dtype=torch.float16. Since dtype is part of the fixed input specification, the mutated code path is completely unreachable during testing, making the original and mutant behaviorally identical for all float32 inputs regardless of their numerical values.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutant cannot be killed under the fixed test configuration. The mutation affects only the half-precision kernel specialization, but the input dtype is fixed at float32 which uses the unmutated generic template. Killing this mutant would require changing the input dtype to float16, which violates the fixed input specification.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing CUDA kernels with type-specialized templates, ensure that the test configuration includes inputs of ALL supported dtypes (float16, float32, float64). The AT_DISPATCH macro creates distinct code paths per dtype, and a mutation in one specialization can go undetected if that dtype is excluded from testing. Consider adding dtype coverage as an explicit dimension in test generation.
